{{lb|en|ergative|slang}} Usually with "up", to [[inform]] or [[learn]]. #: {{ux|en|Mo '''wised''' him up about his situation.}} #: {{ux|en|After Mo had a word with him, he '''wised''' up.}} ===Etymology 2=== From {{inh|en|enm|wise}}, from {{inh|en|ang|wīse}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*wīsō}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|wijze}}, {{cog|de|Weise}}, {{cog|no|vis}}, {{cog|sv|visa}}, {{m|sv|vis}}, {{cog|it|guisa}}, {{cog|es|guisa}}. Compare {{m|en|-wise}}. {{dbt|en|guise}}. ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # {{senseid|en|manner}} {{lb|en|archaic}} [[way|Way]], [[manner]], or [[method]]. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1481|author=w:William Caxton|title=The History of Reynard the Fox|url=https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Historye_of_Reynard_the_Foxe/capitulo_.primo._(2) |passage=In such '''wise''' that all the beasts, great and small, came to the court save Reynard the Fox.}} #* {{RQ:KJV|Matthew|1|18|passage=Now the birth of Iesus Christ was on this '''wise''': When as his mother Mary was espoused to Ioseph (before they came together) shee was found with childe of the holy Ghost.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1850|author=w:Dante Gabriel Rossetti|title=The Burden of Nineveh|lines=2–5|passage={{...}} the prize
Dead Greece vouchsafes to living eyes, —
Her Art for ever in fresh '''wise'''
From hour to hour rejoicing me.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1866|author=w:Algernon Swinburne|title=A Ballad of Life|lines=28–30 |passage=A riven hood was pulled across his eyes;
The token of him being upon this '''wise'''
Made for a sign of Lust.}} #* {{RQ:Gandhi Experiments|volume=I|chapter=xviii|passage=Meantime a serious question came up for discussion.{{...}}The discussion arose somewhat in this '''wise'''. The President of the Society was Mr. Hills, proprietor of the Thames Iron Works. He was a puritan. {{...|It may be said that the existence of the Society depended practically on his financial assistance. Many members of the Committee were more or less his protégés. Dr. Allinson of vegetarian fame was also a member of the Committee. He was an advocate of the then new birth control movement, and preached its methods among the working classes. Mr. Hills regarded these methods as cutting at the root of morals. He thought that the Vegetarian Society had for its object not only dietetic but also moral reform, and that a man of Dr. Allinson's anti-puritanic views should not be allowed to remain in the Society. A motion was therefore brought for his removal.}}}} =====Derived terms===== * {{l|en|-wise}} * {{l|en|alwise}} * {{l|en|nowise}} ===Etymology 3=== {{etymid|en|advise}} From {{inh|en|enm|wisen|t=to advise, direct}}, from {{inh|en|ang|wisian|t=to show the way, guide, direct}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*wīsōn}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*wīsōną|t=to show the way, dispense knowledge}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*weyd-|t=to know}}. Compare {{cog|nl|wijzen|t=to indicate, point out}}, {{cog|de|weisen|t=to show, indicate}}, {{cog|da|-}} and {{cog|nb|vise|t=to show}}, {{cog|nn|visa|t=to show}}. ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # {{lb|en|dialectal}} To [[instruct]]. # {{lb|en|dialectal}} To [[advise]]; [[induce]]. # {{lb|en|dialectal}} To [[show]] the way, [[guide]]. # {{lb|en|dialectal}} To [[direct]] the course of, [[pilot]]. # {{lb|en|dialectal}} To [[cause]] to [[turn]]. ===Anagrams=== * {{anagrams|en|a=eisw|Siew|wies}} {{C|en|Personality}}
